hypothesis: Formulating Barlow Twins decorrelation across three correlation matrices—inter-view cross-correlation C_12 and intra-view auto-correlations C_11 and C_22—simultaneously penalizes both inter-view cross-channel alignment errors and intra-view channel redundancies. Combining this complete decorrelation regularization with Decoupled Contrastive Loss (DCL) prevents channel redundancy within individual feature representations and maximizes the feature space rank across all 2048 projection dimensions, yielding higher linear probe accuracy.
rationale: Iter 16 introduced joint DCL + Barlow Twins loss on cross-correlation matrix C_12, achieving 0.6200 val_acc (our best score). However, standard Barlow Twins only penalizes C_12. If a single view z1 or z2 contains correlated feature channels (e.g. C_11 off-diagonals != 0), C_12 alone might mask intra-view channel collapse. Extending decorrelation to C_11 and C_22 explicitly forces the feature space to span an orthogonal basis within each individual view as well as across views. This intra- and inter-view decorrelation complements DCL sample-level repulsion without adding computational overhead.
expected_effect: Eliminates intra-view representation redundancy, increases projection space rank, and improves linear-probe top-1 accuracy beyond 0.6200.
change_summary:
1. Refactored BarlowTwinsLoss to compute Tri-Matrix Decorrelation: computes C_12 (cross-view), C_11 (intra-view 1), and C_22 (intra-view 2) auto/cross-correlation matrices. Off-diagonal decorrelation penalties are computed on all three matrices to enforce strict channel orthogonality within and across views.
2. Retained the best anti-aliased ResNet-26 backbone (1.5x width, 768-dim features), 4096-wide projection head, and CIFAR-100 detail-preserving augmentations.
